tagline: Out of Portsmouth into Ohio's Little Smokies.
intro: From downtown Portsmouth, near the floodwall murals, the byway heads west into Shawnee State Forest, the largest in Ohio and known as Ohio's Little Smokies, then swings north to Otway and Rarden and comes back by Duck Run and Lucasville. Building stone was quarried in these hills from the mid-1800s, and most of it went by rail and barge to put up buildings in Cincinnati.
In the 1930s the Civilian Conservation Corps had seven camps in the forest, four of them segregated African American camps, and built most of its roads and five small lakes.

moments.title: Picnic Point
moments.text: From this spot in the state forest the view runs southeast down the Ohio River valley toward Portsmouth.

moments.title: Otway Covered Bridge
moments.text: Built in 1874 by the Smith Bridge Company of Toledo, the 127-foot bridge over Scioto Brush Creek was bypassed in 1961 and kept up after that by the Otway Historical Society.

moments.title: Duck Run
moments.text: On the family farm here young Leonard Slye, later Roy Rogers, learned to ride and to yodel, and he and his mother used different yodels to call to each other across the farm.
